title: Allegheny Airlines 737

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Allegheny Airlines Flight 737 - Convair 440, N5825 Near Bradford, Pennsylvania

location.name: Golf course near Bradford Regional Airport

summary: Allegheny Airlines Flight 737, a Convair CV-580, struck treetops just under five nautical miles from Bradford Regional Airport and crashed upside down on a snow-covered golf course during an instrument approach. Weather was overcast with 1.5 miles visibility and snow showers. Eleven of the 28 occupants on board were killed.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board was unable to determine the probable cause. Three potential causes remained after analysis: misreading of the altimeter by the captain, a malfunction of the captain's altimeter following completion of the instrument approach procedure turn, or misinterpretation of the instrument approach chart.

factors.evidence: Weather was overcast with one and one half miles visibility and snow showers.
Three possible causes examined were misreading of the altimeter by the captain, a malfunction of the captain's altimeter, or misinterpretation of the instrument approach chart.
The aircraft struck treetops just under five nautical miles from the airport, indicating the crew descended below safe altitude.
The flight struck treetops and came to rest upside down on a snow-covered golf course.

events.text: Flight 737 at ten miles from airport requested clearance to make instrument approach to runway 14
Clearance received to make instrument approach to runway 14 instead of runway 32
Aircraft descended on approach under instrument conditions with reduced visibility
Aircraft struck treetops just under five nautical miles from airport
Aircraft came to rest upside down on snow-covered golf course
